papers.title: Gate-dependent offset charge shifts and anharmonicity in gatemon qubits in the weak tunneling regime
papers.abstract: Gatemon qubits are based on a superconductor-quantum dot-superconductor (S-QD-S) junction which enables in situ electrostatic tuning via a gate electrode. For a single-channel QD this structure gives rise to two subgap Andreev bound states (ABSs), and generally leads to a richer quantum phase dynamics as compared to conventional transmons. In a recent work [Phys. Rev. B 111, 214503 (2025)] we derived the quantum phase dynamics from a many-body treatment which leads to an effective gate voltage-dependent Hamiltonian that self-consistently incorporates the phase quantization. It predicts (i) a renormalization of the junction's effective capacitance and (ii) the presence of gate voltage and occupation-dependent charge offsets in junctions with tunneling asymmetry. Here, we quantify the observable impact of these effects on the qubit's energy spectrum and anharmonicity, by studying the interplay of the two Andreev branches as a function of dot-gate voltages and junction transparencies. We show the relation of these predictions to simplified gatemon models and propose a protocol to experimentally detect the predicted charge offsets.

summary.summary: This paper quantifies the observable impact of gate-voltage-dependent capacitance renormalization ($\delta C_\Sigma$) and charge offsets ($\delta n_g$ and $n_z$) on gatemon qubit spectra in the weak tunneling regime ($\Gamma_{L,R} \ll \Delta$), derived from a many-body treatment with self-consistent phase quantization. The main prediction is an effective charge offset shift $\delta n_\mathrm{eff}(\epsilon_g)$ in asymmetric junctions ($\Gamma_L \neq \Gamma_R$) that manifests as an $\epsilon_g$-dependent displacement of charge-parity oscillations in $E_{01}(n_g)$.
summary.motivation: Simplified gatemon models have neglected phase-fluctuation effects in the charging energy, leading to incomplete predictions for energy spectra and anharmonicity, particularly for explaining recently observed anomalous anharmonicity behavior in experiments.
summary.method: Numerical solutions of the Schrödinger equation with the full Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_\mathrm{even}$) including the two Andreev branches and new charging-energy terms, combined with WKB analysis at high transparency ($T \approx 1$) to elucidate the interplay between upper and lower Andreev branches.
summary.result: The capacitance renormalization contributes to anharmonicity comparably to the continuum energy shift $E_\mathrm{cont}(\phi)$ for moderate $\epsilon_g \in (0.1\Delta, 0.7\Delta)$; the effective charge offset $\delta n_\mathrm{eff}(\epsilon_g)$ ranges from a few percent to $\lesssim 0.5 e$ and can be detected spectroscopically by measuring $E_{01}(n_g)$ at varied gate voltages in asymmetric junctions.

papers.title: Architecture-aware Unitary Synthesis
papers.abstract: We present a novel architecture-aware transpilation method for exact general unitary gate synthesis on superconducting quantum hardware. Our approach is tightly integrated with the optimized block-ZXZ decomposition, exploiting its recursive structure to make hardware-aware decisions at each level of the recursion rather than treating transpilation as an independent post-processing step. The method introduces three key techniques: a greedy qubit mapping strategy that minimizes pairwise distances between physical qubits, an adaptive Gray code selection combined with qubit swapping that optimizes the construction of uniformly controlled Rz gates for the target topology, and a heuristic for reducing CNOT gates by exploiting the structure of long-range CNOT ladders. We benchmark our method against TKet, Qiskit, and Pennylane on the 20-qubit IQM Garnet (square lattice) and the 156-qubit IBM Marrakesh (heavy-hex) architectures with qubit counts ranging from 3 to 11. Our method achieves CNOT count reductions of up to 36 percent on the IQM Garnet and up to 34 percent on the IBM Marrakesh compared to the best competing transpiler, while simultaneously achieving transpilation speedups of up to 553x. Furthermore, our method is the only one capable of transpiling circuits beyond 10 qubits within a 30-minute time limit across both architectures.

summary.summary: This work presents a method for architecture-aware transpilation of general $n$-qubit unitary synthesis on superconducting quantum hardware, tightly integrating transpilation with the optimized block-ZXZ decomposition that uses $\Theta(4^n)$ CNOT gates. The method combines greedy qubit mapping, adaptive Gray code selection with qubit swapping, and CNOT-ladder heuristics to achieve 34–36% CNOT reductions versus Qiskit/Pennylane and 553× speedup versus TKET on 20-qubit IQM Garnet (square lattice) and 156-qubit IBM Marrakesh (heavy-hex) platforms for 3–11 qubits.
summary.motivation: Exact synthesis of general unitaries is essential in Hamiltonian simulation, quantum state preparation, QSP/QSVT, and block-encoding subroutines, but existing transpilers treat synthesis and routing as decoupled steps, losing opportunity to exploit the recursive structure of block-ZXZ decomposition for hardware-specific optimization.
summary.method: Architecture-aware transpilation integrates three techniques: (1) greedy qubit mapping minimizing pairwise distance cost $C_{\mathrm{dist}} = \sum_{u,v \in S} d(u,v)$ on the coupling graph; (2) adaptive selection of cyclic Gray codes that assign highest CNOT frequencies $f_{n-1} = 2^{n-2}$ to physically nearby qubits, combined with SWAP optimization; (3) a heuristic exploiting intermediate entanglement in long-range CNOT ladders (requiring $4k-4$ gates for distance $k > 1$) to opportunistically apply $R_z$ gates and merge redundant CNOTs.
summary.result: On IQM Garnet, average CNOT reductions of 27% versus Qiskit and 36% versus Pennylane; on IBM Marrakesh, 19% versus Qiskit and 34% versus Pennylane. Transpilation times scale as $O(|V|^2 + |V| \cdot n + n^2 \cdot 2^n)$, achieving 553× speedup over TKET and enabling successful transpilation of 11-qubit unitaries within 30 minutes where TKET and Pennylane failed beyond 8 qubits. CNOT counts exceed the theoretical lower bound by 44% (IQM Garnet) and 58% (IBM Marrakesh) due to routing overhead.
